brief.scenario: Ms Clarke, 42, found a lump in her left breast two weeks ago. A chaperone is available. The breast is represented by a simulator.
brief.task: Examine her breasts. You will be stopped at 6 minutes to present your findings and answer questions.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Chaperone and consent first, normal side first, then the axilla.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Going straight to the lump and forgetting the axilla and supraclavicular nodes.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "Before we start, I'd like to offer you a chaperone."

grid.label: Consent and chaperone
grid.fail: Examines without offering a chaperone or explaining the examination.
grid.pass: Explains the examination, gains consent, offers a chaperone, and records the discussion.
grid.high: Checks her preferences (e.g. a female chaperone) and keeps her covered except for the area being examined.

grid.label: Inspection
grid.fail: Inspects with arms by the sides only.
grid.pass: Sitting: arms by sides, hands pressed on hips, arms above head.
grid.high: Adds leaning forward, and looks for skin tethering, peau d'orange, nipple inversion and asymmetry.

grid.label: Palpation
grid.fail: Palpates only the lump, or starts with the symptomatic side.
grid.pass: Normal side first, patient semi-reclined with arm behind head; flat hand, all quadrants, axillary tail, nipple.
grid.high: Uses a systematic pattern and tests the lump for fixation to skin and chest wall (pectoralis tensed).

grid.label: Lymph nodes
grid.pass: Examines the axilla with the arm supported, and the supraclavicular fossae.
grid.high: Examines each axillary group: apical, central, anterior, posterior, lateral.

grid.label: Presentation at the signal
grid.fail: Lists actions rather than findings, or runs past the signal.
grid.borderline: Describes the lump but not whether it is fixed.
grid.pass: Describes the lump (site, size, shape, consistency, mobility) and nodes, then gives a most likely diagnosis.
grid.high: Leads with the key finding, states the important negatives, and names the concern directly.

grid.label: Next steps
grid.pass: Triple assessment: clinical examination, imaging and core biopsy.
grid.high: States suspected cancer pathway referral for an unexplained lump at 30 or over, or nipple changes in one nipple at 50 or over.

grid.label: Closing
grid.fail: Leaves her exposed or doesn't explain what happens next.
grid.pass: Thanks her, lets her dress in privacy, explains next steps, and records the chaperone's name.
grid.high: Checks her understanding and concerns before leaving.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Starts examining the left breast without mentioning a chaperone.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Inspects with her arms by her sides, then palpates the lump only.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: There's a lump. I felt it and it's probably a cyst.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: It's probably nothing; she can come back if it grows.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Hello, I'm Dr Patel. Can I confirm your name and date of birth? I'd like to examine both breasts and the glands in your armpits and neck. I'd like to offer you a chaperone; would you like one? [Chaperone present; cleans hands.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Could you sit with your arms by your sides… now press your hands on your hips… now raise your arms above your head.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Could you lie back with your right arm behind your head? I'll start with the right side. [Flat hand, all quadrants, axillary tail, nipple; then the left.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Supports her arm and examines the axilla; then the supraclavicular fossae.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Thank you. Please take your time to get dressed. I'll explain what happens next. [Records chaperone's name.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Ms Clarke has a 2 cm hard, irregular lump in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast, not fixed to skin or chest wall, with a palpable mobile left axillary node. This is concerning for breast carcinoma.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Triple assessment: clinical examination, imaging and a core biopsy.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Hello, I'm Dr Patel. Can I confirm your name and date of birth? I'd like to look at and feel both breasts, and the glands in your armpits and above the collarbones. I'd like to offer a chaperone; would you prefer a female colleague? You'll stay covered except for the part I'm examining. [Cleans hands.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Arms by your sides… hands pressing on your hips… arms above your head… and could you lean forward for me? [Looks for tethering, peau d'orange, nipple inversion, asymmetry.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Normal side first, systematically, then the left.] Could you press your hand into your hip while I feel the lump? [Tests fixation to pectoralis and skin.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Each axillary group: apical, central, anterior, posterior, lateral; then supraclavicular.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Thank you. Take your time to dress, and then we'll talk about what happens next. Is there anything worrying you? [Records chaperone's name.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The key finding is a 2 cm hard, irregular lump in the left upper outer quadrant, not fixed to skin or pectoralis, with a mobile left axillary node. There's no skin change or nipple change, and no supraclavicular nodes. I'm concerned this is breast carcinoma.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Triple assessment with imaging and core biopsy, through a suspected cancer pathway, which applies to anyone 30 or over with an unexplained breast lump.

failures.consequence: Undoes the dignity the chaperone and consent were meant to protect.

failures.move: Not saying whether the lump is fixed.
failures.consequence: Fixation to skin or chest wall changes staging and surgery.

failures.move: Skipping the axilla and supraclavicular fossae.
failures.consequence: Misses nodal disease that changes staging and the operation.

recovery.when: You started without offering a chaperone
recovery.line: I'm sorry, before I go on I should have offered you a chaperone. Would you like one?
Before I finish, I'd like to examine the glands in your armpits and above your collarbones.

knowledge.fact: Offer a chaperone, explain the examination, gain consent, and record the discussion and the chaperone's identity.
Suspected cancer pathway: aged 30 or over with an unexplained breast lump; aged 50 or over with discharge, retraction or other concerning change in one nipple.
Triple assessment: clinical examination, imaging, and core biopsy.

recall.think: Dignity first; is the lump fixed; where are the nodes?
recall.say: "I'd like to offer you a chaperone."
do: Inspect in three positions, then leaning forward
recall.finish: Triple assessment via a suspected cancer pathway.

partner.opening: Please examine this patient's breasts. A chaperone is available. I'll stop you at 6 minutes.
partner.actorBrief: You are Ms Clarke, 42. You found the lump in the shower two weeks ago. You're anxious and would prefer a female chaperone if asked. No nipple discharge, no pain. If asked: your aunt had breast cancer at 60.

reveals.finding: No asymmetry, skin changes or nipple inversion.
2 cm hard, irregular lump, upper outer quadrant; not fixed to skin or pectoralis.
One firm, mobile node in the central group.
Say: "Please stop there and present your findings."

push.question: What is your most likely diagnosis?
What happens next?
push.expect: Triple assessment via a suspected cancer pathway.

curveballs.safeAnswer: Respect her choice, explain, and record the discussion; if uncomfortable proceeding, offer to rearrange.

curveballs.prompt: She's 25 with a smooth, mobile lump.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Under 30: non-urgent referral is the NICE default, but still assess fully.
